newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian worker killed by Israeli farmer.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian worker killed by Israeli farmer.

text.p: An Israeli farmer shot and killed a Palestinian worker he suspected was trying to break into his house in southern Israel before dawn on Thursday, a police spokeswoman said.

But members of Samir Abu Shaqfa's family at Gaza's Jabalya refugee camp believed the 40-year-old man was killed to avenge the fatal shooting of a Jewish settler woman and her 12-year-old son by Arab guerrillas in the West Bank one day earlier.

"This was in revenge for the Ramallah attack," said Nabil Abu Shaqfa, a cousin of Samir. "He (Samir) had never been accused of any offence, neither during Israeli rule nor under the Palestinian Authority," he said.
An Israeli police spokeswoman said a 56-year-old Israeli farmer was detained for questioning over the shooting, which took place at the Kochav Michael farming village.

"He said he heard strange voices coming from outside. He said he thought somebody was trying to break in. So he took his gun and went outside and fired at them. They tried to flee but one of them fell," the spokeswoman said.
She said the shooting was from a distance of a few metres (yards) and it appeared the Arab had once worked for his killer.

Israel's domestic news agency Itim reported the dead man was one of three Palestinians brought to the village from Gaza in the early morning by the farmer's neighbour. It said they were walking towards the fields when the shots rang out.

Palestinians, who immediately set up a wake for Abu Shaqfa proclaiming him a "martyr killed by settler herds", said three other Palestinian workers were wounded in the shooting. But Israeli police said they could not confirm others were wounded.
The official Palestinian news agency, in a commentary on the incident, said the shooting was premeditated and accused the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of encouraging such attacks.

"The killer...was not mad but someone who had been encouraged and pushed to do his act. He knows that his sentence would be an honour and that he would perhaps be listed among Israel's heroes," the commentary in a dispatch by WAFA news agency said.
Ziad al-Atrash, a senior Palestinian police officer in Gaza, said his information discounted the possibility that the man was killed on suspicion of burglary.
"I don't want to pre-empt events, but the information I have does not match the claim that the workers were on a robbery," Atrash told Reuters.
Atrash, head of the Palestinian side of a liaison committee with Israel, said he had asked for a joint investigation.
Itim said the farmer initially told police he believed the worker was a thief but later said he thought the Arab was a "terrorist" about to carry out an attack.
"I heard voices in Arabic and thought they were terrorists. I shouted at them to stop. They ran away and then I shot," Itim quoted the farmer as telling police investigators.
